Class ServerConnectionLifecycle

java.lang.Object
it.polimi.ingsoft.mesos.server.network.connectionHandling.ServerConnectionLifecycle
public class ServerConnectionLifecycle extends Object
Handles the lifecycle of server-side client sessions.

This class centralizes the operations that are about the connection itself: registering a new session, recording keep-alive replies, reacting to timeouts, and starting the correct disconnection flow. It is used by virtual views for normal connection operations and by PingPongRoutine when a session no longer answers to ping messages.

The lifecycle service does not own sockets and does not execute lobby or game rules. It reads and updates connection state through ServerSessionRegistry. When a disconnected session belongs to a lobby or a game, it delegates the disconnection to the proper controller by enqueueing a SystemDisconnectCommand. This keeps phase-specific cleanup inside the controller that owns that phase.

    • ServerConnectionLifecycle

      public ServerConnectionLifecycle(ServerSessionRegistry sessions)
      Creates a lifecycle service backed by the shared session registry.

      The constructor also builds and starts the PingPongRoutine that monitors connection timeouts for the registered sessions.

      Parameters:
      sessions - registry containing session state, phase, controllers, and network connections
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if sessions is null

  • Method Details

    • registerConnection

      public String registerConnection(ClientConnection connection)
      Registers a newly accepted client connection and returns its session id.

      The connection is stored in the session registry under a freshly generated session id. When the connection also implements Listener, the registry can later expose it as the session listener so that pre-lobby errors and responses can be sent back to the client.

      Parameters:
      connection - network connection associated with the client
      Returns:
      unique session id assigned by the registry
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if connection is null

    • recordPong

      public void recordPong(String sessionId)
      Records that a client session answered the keep-alive ping.

      The method only updates the timestamp stored in the registry. Timeout detection is performed later by PingPongRoutine using registry snapshots.

      Parameters:
      sessionId - session that sent a pong response

    • disconnectSession

      public void disconnectSession(String sessionId)
      Starts the disconnection flow for a session.

      The current phase is read from the registry snapshot. Game and lobby sessions are not removed directly here: a SystemDisconnectCommand is enqueued to the controller that owns that phase, so the phase-specific model can decide how to clean up the player. Sessions outside lobby and game are unregistered immediately. If no snapshot exists for the session, the method returns without doing anything.

      Parameters:
      sessionId - session to disconnect

    • handleConnectionTimeout

      public void handleConnectionTimeout(String sessionId)
      Handles a keep-alive timeout detected by the ping-pong routine.

      The method first asks the registered ClientConnection to close, then reuses the normal disconnection flow. Exceptions are ignored because timeout handling is already a recovery path and the session may have disappeared while the routine was processing an old snapshot.

      Parameters:
      sessionId - timed-out session
